rulings.docket_item: P02-006 (c04 escalation, OL sub-claim): byte-identical inclusio and the barah lexeme straddle the row's back seam at Song.6.9|6.10 undisclosed; contested consequence - does the praise frame close at WEB 6:9 or extend to WEB 6:10, there being no tier-1 voice-shift marker at that join?
rulings.decision: ADOPT the respan. The praise frame closes at WEB 6:10. P02-006 becomes Song.6.4-Song.6.10 and the standalone row at Song.6.10-Song.6.10 (P02-007) is DISSOLVED into it. The rival reading - that WEB 6:10 OPENS a movement on the strength of the mi-zot anchor - is REFUTED on the count object: the attested opener is the ascent run, and MT 6:10 does not carry it.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently from the pointed bytes, not reproduced from the packet. (1) THE CUT HAS NO TIER-1 MARKER. A word-final-kaf surface audit across the neighbourhood returns MT 6:4 = 0, 6:5 = 2, 6:6 = 1, 6:7 = 2 (the verse closing on לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ, oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier), 6:8 = 0, 6:9 = 0, 6:10 = 0, 6:11 = 0: no 2fs address form stands on either side of the 6:9|6:10 join, and no gendered form CHANGES there - MT 6:9 predicates אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) in the third feminine singular and MT 6:10 continues feminine-singular predication with הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier). No vocative, no imperative onset, no addressee shift. Under the hybrid granularity rule a sustained single-voice run may not be cut without a tier-1 marker AT the cut, and there is none. (2) THE CLOSE IS BYTE-ARGUED. אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת closes oshb:Song.6.4 and closes oshb:Song.6.10 at BYTE tier - exact codepoint identity including accents, re-collated here - and the book-wide byte sweep of that run returns exactly 2 verses (MT 6:4, MT 6:10). That is an inclusio bracketing the unit's own opening verse יָפָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.6.4, byte tier, the rayati vocative plus the 2fs pronoun that carries the front seam) with its candidate closing verse, and refrain/inclusio brackets are a tier-1 driver class. The hybrid rule's clause that refrain verses close units with bracket function ARGUED FROM BYTES is satisfied in its own terms: MT 6:10 is a listed refrain site and its bracket function is carried by a byte-tier identity with the unit's opener, not asserted. (3) TIER CORRECTION TO THE ESCALATING PACKET. The barah pair is NOT byte-identical and must not be cited as though it were: בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא (oshb:Song.6.9) against בָּרָה֙ (oshb:Song.6.10) differ in accent, so the recurrence holds at SKELETON tier only. It is corroboration for continuity across the seam, never the driver; the byte-tier inclusio is the driver. (4) THE CONTROLLING COUNT OBJECT AND ITS DIGIT PAIR. The packets weigh a 3-verse mi-zot figure against a 2-verse one; the controlling object is the ASCENT RUN מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר, skeleton sweep 2 verses (MT 3:6, MT 8:5 - מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר at oshb:Song.8.5), and MT 6:10 is NOT a member of it: MT 6:10 reads הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה with no ascent language. The 3-verse digit counts a different object, the bare two-word interrogative mi-zot (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5). Digit pair: 2 (ascent run) vs 3 (bare interrogative). Since the opener function attested at MT 3:6 and MT 8:5 belongs to the ascent run and MT 6:10 does not carry it, the opener rival rests on the blended object and fails. The bare interrogative is a skeleton-tier pattern, not one of the formula anchors the voice policy enumerates as tier-1, so it cannot be the sole driver of a seam. (5) THE RESULTING SPAN IS TIER-1 BOUNDED ON BOTH EDGES. Front 6:3|6:4: the rayati vocative plus 2fs pronoun at יָפָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.6.4, byte tier) against the mutual-belonging refrain closing oshb:Song.6.3. Back 6:10|6:11: third-feminine-singular predication giving way to first-person narration יָרַ֔דְתִּי (oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) - a genuine person-form seam. (6) TIER-3 CANNOT AND DOES NOT DECIDE THIS. The parashah inventory carries SAMEKH at BOTH MT 6:9 and MT 6:10 (single-witness); marking both sides, it breaks no tie in either direction and is recorded as corroboration only. Absence is never counterevidence anywhere in this ruling.

consequence.spec: P02-006 - RESPAN span to 'Song.6.4-Song.6.10'. Install, in one edit: (a) the back-seam close argued from the inclusio, splicing אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת from BOTH oshb:Song.6.4 and oshb:Song.6.10 and naming the tier as byte with the book-wide sweep digit (byte sweep: 2 verses); (b) the barah recurrence disclosed at SKELETON tier explicitly, never as byte-identity; (c) the c04 both-primaries cure that already stood on this row - delete the byte-false absence claim from boundary_rationale AND from strongest_rejected_alternative and replace it with the audited person-form facts (2fs address forms present MT 6:5-6:7, absent MT 6:8-6:10; MT 6:9 third-feminine-singular predication with 1cs-possessive epithets), arguing the wider bound POSITIVELY rather than by denying a marker; (d) the migrated c04 P02-007 cures, which this row now owns because it now owns MT 6:10 - tier-label the mi-zot recurrence as skeleton (sweep: 3 verses for the bare interrogative) and strike the word 'ascending' from any label applied to MT 6:10, whose bytes carry no ascent verb (ascent-run object, skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5); (e) span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry, now unconditional on the wider span - the SAMEKH at MT 6:9 is span-INTERNAL and the SAMEKH at MT 6:10 sits at the new back edge; disclose both, single-witness, corroboration only. DEPENDENT FIELDS re-opened by the span change and the driver swap: unit_type (re-argue from the merged bytes with the one-sentence deviation disclosure the operative-category law requires, since the row now closes on a third-feminine-singular interrogative rather than on body-part address), observed_substrate_signals (re-cut to the surviving drivers using the dotted taxonomy), strongest_rejected_alternative (the live rival is now the 6:4-6:9 cut this ruling rejects, engaged on the ascent-run count object), boundary_evidence_refs, and confidence (re-open; cap at medium_low - the frame is contested and the internal 6:7|6:8 join remains unmarked). P02-007 - DISSOLVED. Remove the row; its span is absorbed. Its two upheld c04 defects do not vanish with it: both are carried onto P02-006 by (d) above. P02-008 - CONSEQUENCE ROW, must be touched. It is now the ONLY row that can argue the 6:10|6:11 seam, because the row that formerly argued that join is dissolved: add the front-seam argument with both sides spliced and tier-labelled (third-feminine-singular predication at oshb:Song.6.10 against יָרַ֔דְתִּי at oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier), add web:Song.6.10 to boundary_evidence_refs, and re-cut the sentence that calls web:Song.6.10 'the immediately preceding verse' closing under a setumah, since MT 6:10 is now the closing verse of the preceding ROW and the disclosure must say so. NOT a consequence row, stated so the author wave does not edit it speculatively: P02-005 (Song.6.1-Song.6.3) - its back seam 6:3|6:4 is untouched by this ruling. Chunk ordinals renumber at assembly. TESTS each cure must pass - the tests that killed the originals: (i) a word-final-kaf plus 1cs/3fs audit over MT 6:4-6:10 must not contradict any person-form or absence wording left anywhere on the row; (ii) every recurrence sentence names its object AND its tier, and no byte-identity wording survives on the barah pair; (iii) no element of a formula label may be asserted that a sweep of the labelled verse's own bytes cannot find; (iv) delete every setumah sentence and the new back seam must still stand on the inclusio alone.

rulings.docket_item: P02-018 + P02-017 SEAM-PAIR (c06 escalation): the Song.8.5|8.6 front-seam 'voice shift' misdescribes the bytes; escalated because the closed vocabulary names the 8:6-7 peak as the epigram exemplar while the granularity rule bars an unmarked cut inside a sustained single-voice run.
rulings.decision: ADOPT the merge. The Song.8.5|8.6 cut is STRUCK. P02-018 is respanned to Song.8.5-Song.8.7 and P02-017 is DISSOLVED into it - ONE edit, installed on both rows. The owner's category assignment is PRESERVED: epigram_unit remains the operative type for the love-strong-as-death peak; what changes is the row's span, not its category. Ratifying the cut on the speech-act change is not available to me and is expressly declined.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the pointed bytes. (1) NO TIER-1 MARKER AT THE CUT. A word-final-kaf audit returns MT 8:5 = 4 second-person tokens and MT 8:6 = 2, and every one of the six is final kaf plus qamats, i.e. 2ms: עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ and יְלָדַֽתְךָ (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier) continue directly into לִבֶּ֗ךָ and זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier). שִׂימֵ֨נִי (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) is a masculine-singular imperative carrying a 1cs object suffix, so BOTH the speaker (1cs) and the addressee (2ms) are unchanged across the seam. No gendered form changes; no vocative or imperative onset marks a turn to a new addressee; no attested formula anchor stands at the join. What changes is mood and speech act, and the row's front-seam signal naming that a voice shift is byte-false. The address chain straddling the seam is a byte-true device undisclosed on either row, which argues continuity against the cut. (2) THE ONLY AVAILABLE RATIFYING GROUND IS BARRED TO ME. Ratifying the cut would rest on the marked speech-act change plus the named category. A speech-act or mood change is not a member of the tier-1 set the voice policy enumerates (gendered suffixes and verb forms, vocatives, attested formula anchors); it is tier-2. The owner addendum symmetry binds a ruling exactly as it binds a challenge or a defence, so a tier-2-only ground cannot carry a boss ratification, and marker absence is never counterevidence in the other direction either. Admitting the speech-act class as tier-1 would be legislating a new marker category, which is outside my authority. (3) THE PERCEIVED COLLISION WITH THE CLOSED VOCABULARY DISSOLVES ON THE VOCABULARY'S OWN TEXT, so this does not require reinterpreting the law and is not escalated. The unit_type section names candidate ZONES whose bounds are writer-argued, by its own wording: the descriptive-poem entry says bounds are writer-argued and prints one of its zones with a literal question mark; the bracket-verse entry directs that bracket function be argued from bytes; the epigram entry closes on units 'argued from bytes'. Those lines assign CATEGORIES and identify which text carries the form; they do not fix row spans against the granularity rule. Reading them otherwise would also have forbidden the respan this same ledger adopts at the 6:4-6:9 zone, which the section itself marks as open. Accordingly the category survives untouched and the span follows the bytes. (4) THE MERGED SPAN IS TIER-1 BOUNDED ON BOTH EDGES. Front 8:4|8:5: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Song.8.4, byte tier) is an attested oath formula anchor with the daughters vocative - tier-1 - and across the join oshb:Song.8.5 opens on the attested ascent run מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5) in a third-feminine-singular voice. Back 8:7|8:8: אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) opens a first-person-PLURAL speaker group against the singular voices preceding - a genuine speaker change. The word-final-kaf audit returns 0 for MT 8:7 and 0 for MT 8:8, so no address form competes at that edge. (5) NO INTERNAL JOIN IS BEING SUPPRESSED. Within the merged span the 8:6|8:7 join was already held whole and unchallenged; the audit returns MT 8:7 = 0 second-person tokens, the verse turning gnomic without any gendered form changing, so nothing of the tier-1 class sits there either. The one real shift inside the span is INTRA-VERSE, in MT 8:5, from the third-feminine-singular question to the 1cs/2ms address - and an intra-verse turn cannot be a row boundary at verse granularity, so it is a disclosure duty, not a cut. (6) TIER-3, RECORDED AS CORROBORATION ONLY. The parashah inventory places SAMEKH at MT 8:4 and at MT 8:7 and NONE between, so the layer brackets MT 8:5-8:7 as one seg block and the merged row closes on a seg. Single-witness, never a driver; it corroborates, and it would not have been permitted to decide.

consequence.spec: ONE seam-pair edit - the deletion of the Song.8.5|8.6 cut - installed on both rows as follows. P02-018 - RESPAN span to 'Song.8.5-Song.8.7'. Install: (a) deletion of the byte-false front-seam voice-shift signal and of the signal key that carries it; (b) the front seam re-argued at 8:4|8:5 with both sides spliced and tier-labelled (הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם at oshb:Song.8.4, byte tier, against מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר at oshb:Song.8.5, skeleton sweep: 2 verses); (c) disclosure of the 1cs/2ms address chain now running INSIDE the row - עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ and יְלָדַֽתְךָ (oshb:Song.8.5) through שִׂימֵ֨נִי, לִבֶּ֗ךָ, זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6), byte tier - stating that no gendered form changes across the former join, which is why the cut was struck; (d) disclosure of the intra-verse turn in MT 8:5 from the third-feminine-singular question to the 1cs/2ms address, held not resolved; (e) the migrated c06 P02-017 cures, which this row now owns: re-cut the blended mi-zot digit so each citation names exactly one object (bare interrogative, sweep: 3 verses; ascent run, sweep: 2 verses) and re-anchor the cross-row reference to named verses rather than to the treatment of other sites; (f) the already-upheld c06 quote/gloss parity cure on this row - either extend the spliced run to include the causal particle that opens the clause at oshb:Song.8.6 or drop 'for' from the gloss, re-collating at byte tier; (g) the tier-3 disclosure that the mark layer places no seg between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7 and that the row closes on the MT 8:7 seg, single-witness, corroboration only. DEPENDENT FIELDS re-opened: unit_type - KEEP epigram_unit as the operative category, and add the one-sentence deviation disclosure the operative-category law requires, since the row now opens on the ascent formula and an address chain before reaching the aphoristic peak; observed_substrate_signals (re-cut to the surviving drivers); strongest_rejected_alternative (the live rival is now the 8:5|8:6 cut this ruling strikes, engaged on the absence of any tier-1 marker at it, NOT on the chapter or on a 'fresh movement'); boundary_evidence_refs (add web:Song.8.4 and web:Song.8.8 as the seam neighbours); confidence (re-open; cap at medium_low - the MT 8:6 shalhevet-yah crux stays held and the merged frame is contested). The shalhevet-yah crux handling that c06 certified must be carried across the merge intact: divided-token fact disclosed, construal held, no standalone divine-name digit. P02-017 - DISSOLVED. Remove the row; its span is absorbed by P02-018. Its upheld c06 cures do not vanish with it - they are carried by (e) above. P02-016 - CONSEQUENCE ROW, must be touched, and only for this: its strongest_rejected_alternative and its boundary_evidence_refs name the neighbouring movement by the span 'web:Song.8.1-Song.8.3', which ceases to exist under B-4. Re-name the preceding neighbour to the span B-4 adopts. Its own boundary at 8:3|8:4 is NOT disturbed by this ruling and must not be re-opened. NOT a consequence row, stated so it is not edited speculatively: P02-019 (Song.8.8-Song.8.9) - its seam pair 8:7|8:8 and its only neighbour ref, oshb:Song.8.7, are unchanged by the merge. Chunk ordinals renumber at assembly. TESTS each cure must pass - the tests that killed the originals: (i) remove the words naming a mood or speech-act change and the front seam must still stand on a gender-marked form or an attested formula anchor that CHANGES at the seam; (ii) no seam claim may rest on a device that runs unbroken across it undisclosed; (iii) every count citation names exactly one object; (iv) every English gloss translates only what its Hebrew run contains, and every spliced run re-collates at byte tier against its own cited ref.

rulings.docket_item: P02-013 (c05 peer boundary proposal, held with its cures): the mutual-belonging verse web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 - the peer found the front seam tier-1-arguable but no arguable FORWARD driver, and proposed merging the verse forward into P02-014.
rulings.decision: DECLINE the merge proposal; P02-013 STANDS as its own unit at Song.7.10-Song.7.10. The peer's premise that no tier-1 driver sits at the forward seam is REFUTED on the bytes: an imperative-plus-vocative onset and an addressee shift stand at oshb:Song.7.11 | oshb:Song.7.12 (= web:Song.7.10 | web:Song.7.11), and both classes are tier-1 drivers. The row's held cures are converted into phase-2 orders and are enumerated below.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the pointed bytes; the peer's own front-seam finding is sustained and its forward-seam finding is corrected. (1) FRONT SEAM - TIER-1, AS THE PEER FOUND. A word-final-kaf audit with the roles split returns genuine 2fs address forms at MT 7:9 (שָׁדַ֨יִךְ֙ and אַפֵּ֖ךְ, oshb:Song.7.9 = web:Song.7.8, byte tier) and at MT 7:10 (וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ, oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9, byte tier), and ZERO at MT 7:11. The audit's other final-kaf hit in MT 7:10 must be role-split out and not counted as an address form: הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9, byte tier) carries a root-final kaf, not a 2fs suffix. So the man's 2fs address stops and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier) opens her 1cs voice on an attested mutual-belonging refrain - a formula anchor the voice policy enumerates as tier-1. The row argues this seam from imagery class instead, which is the defect the peer upheld and which the cure must repair. (2) FORWARD SEAM - THE PEER'S PREMISE IS REFUTED. Across oshb:Song.7.11 | oshb:Song.7.12 (= web:Song.7.10 | web:Song.7.11) the speaker does not change, and the peer stopped there. But the ADDRESSEE does: MT 7:11 speaks ABOUT him in the third masculine singular, closing on the 3ms suffix of אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier), while MT 7:12 turns and speaks TO him, opening לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.7.12 = web:Song.7.11, byte tier) - a 2ms imperative onset carrying the dodi vocative. Vocative and imperative onsets and addressee shifts are tier-1 driver classes, and the dodi address vocabulary is an enumerated tier-1 anchor. A qualifying marker therefore does sit at the forward seam; the merge proposal's condition ('if no forward driver can be argued') is not met, so it does not trigger. (3) THE DEVICE THAT STRADDLES BOTH SEAMS IS A ROLE SPLIT, NOT A COUNTEREXAMPLE, AND MUST BE DISCLOSED. The dod lexeme runs through the seam in a changed speech role - referential at MT 7:11, vocative at MT 7:12 - which is precisely the marker, not an argument against it. Naming the controlling count object as the ruling requires: the object is 'verses carrying a dod-lexeme token of any attested spelling', 5 consecutive MT verses, MT 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:13, 7:14 (= web:Song.7.9, 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:13), the MT 7:13 member being the defective דֹּדַ֖י (oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12, byte tier). Digit pair and why they differ: 5 for that object against 28 for the prefix-tolerant dod-family object, which does NOT contain MT 7:13 because the defective spelling escapes it, and against 24 for dodi-exact. The chain STOPS at MT 7:14: MT 8:1 carries no dod token at all, which is why it plays no part in B-4. (4) WHAT THE ROW MAY NOT LEAN ON. The parashah inventory does carry SAMEKH at MT 7:11 = web:Song.7.10 under the claimed type, and the row rests its forward seam on it and on nothing else. In the Writings that layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver; it is disclosed single-witness and demoted to corroboration by the cure. The row argues the seam that did not need arguing and left driverless the one that did - both are repaired below.

consequence.spec: P02-013 - span UNCHANGED at 'Song.7.10-Song.7.10' (full X-X form retained). The peer's held cures become phase-2 orders, installed as one edit: (a) boundary_rationale must argue the FRONT seam from its tier-1 markers with spliced byte-tier forms on both sides - אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10) against the man's 2fs wasf address וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ (oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9) - replacing the imagery-class and derived-boundary appeal entirely; (b) it must SUPPLY the forward driver this ruling identifies rather than record that none exists: splice לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.7.12 = web:Song.7.11, byte tier) as an imperative-plus-vocative onset and name the addressee shift from third-person reference to direct address across the seam; (c) disclose the dod-lexeme chain straddling BOTH seams with the object named per attested spelling and its digit (5 consecutive MT verses, MT 7:10-7:14 = web:Song.7.9-7:13), naming the speech-role split - referential at MT 7:11, vocative at MT 7:12 - so the straddle is shown to carry the marker rather than to contradict it; (d) demote the setumah to corroboration only, single-witness, never the forward warrant; (e) verse-anchor the unanchored mutual-belonging cross-row reference in device_notes and mirror the named verses into boundary_evidence_refs - this is one of the three instances of the unanchored-reference class in this part and must be run as a SWEEP with the others, not as a spot fix, since an unanchored reference evades the mirror check by construction and a GREEN re-run alone does not certify the cure; (f) the apostrophe repair on the curly WEB quotation, cured by the three-site sweep already ordered on this cluster and not re-litigated here. REFUTED and NOT to be installed: the epigram_unit relabel - the bytes carry an attested refrain member quoted at its own shape, not an aphorism - and any weighing of the co-located setumah against unit_type, which inverts the tier. unit_type stays lyric_address. Offset-zone Tier-0 discipline binds every structured ref written anywhere on this row, in prose fields as well as in boundary_evidence_refs. TESTS the cure must pass: (i) delete every setumah sentence and BOTH seams must still stand on their own spliced, tier-labelled evidence - the support that was doing all the work in the original; (ii) every cross-row reference resolves to a named verse that also appears in boundary_evidence_refs, verified by hand and not by a GREEN mirror run; (iii) every dod digit names its object and its spelling before it is written.

rulings.docket_item: P02-015 (c05, HIGH, both primaries): the row cuts a continuous single-voice run at the WEB chapter 7|8 boundary with no tier-1 marker at the cut and never engages the live merger rival with the preceding row P02-014.
rulings.decision: ADOPT the merge. P02-014 is respanned to Song.7.11-Song.8.3, absorbing P02-015, which is DISSOLVED. The cut at web:Song.7.13 | web:Song.8.1 (= oshb:Song.7.14 | oshb:Song.8.1) is struck: it falls on a chapter division, which is tier-4 and never boundary evidence, and carries no tier-1 marker of any class.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the pointed bytes; the two primaries converge and are sustained. (1) NO TIER-1 MARKER AT THE CUT. Neither speaker nor addressee changes across it. MT 7:14 closes דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ (oshb:Song.7.14 = web:Song.7.13, byte tier) - her 1cs perfect under the dodi vocative standing in that same verse, the pausal second-person form being disambiguated as 2ms by that in-verse vocative and by both witnesses' renderings rather than by the surface form alone - and MT 8:1 continues מִ֤י יִתֶּנְךָ֙, אֶֽמְצָאֲךָ֤ and אֶשָׁ֣קְךָ֔ (oshb:Song.8.1, byte tier), 1cs verbs carrying 2ms object suffixes. A word-final-kaf audit returns MT 7:14 = 1 (2ms) and MT 8:1 = 3 (all 2ms): no gendered form changes, no vocative or imperative onset opens MT 8:1, no attested formula anchor stands at the join. A wish construction is not a member of the tier-1 marker set. Two rows both typed lyric_address, both her voice addressing him, were cut apart with no qualifying driver, and neither row engaged the merger: the preceding row declined only an internal split, this row declined only the forward extension into the oath verse. (2) THE AGGRAVATING FACT. The cut falls exactly on the WEB chapter 7|8 division - tier-4 metadata, never boundary evidence - and the row's own warrant words it as a 'fresh movement'.
